methods_note: PREDICATE PROXY — LABELED IMPERFECT. The raw oracle panel (accel_z, vel_1w, vel_3m from engine/oracle/panel.py) is NOT available in this worktree; only Time Machine tile data (rs_ratio, rs_mom per date per node) is committed. Tile rs_mom = vel_1w - vel_3m = accel (the raw, un-normalized velocity difference), confirmed by panel.py code. However, panel.py applies WEEKS velocity divisors that change the magnitude of accel before z-scoring. When we z-score the tile rs_mom over a 252-day window, the resulting accel_z has a DIFFERENT scale than the FSM's true accel_z — measured: only 37.3% (133/357) of catalog onset dates have tile-based accel_z_5d >= 1.0 at the onset date (mean=0.72, median=0.77 vs threshold=1.0), confirming the proxy fires at a different (higher absolute accel) threshold than the FSM. Therefore: the 'first-crossing universe' in this report is NOT the true FSM first-crossings; it is the set of dates where the tile-based accel_z_5d proxy fires. This is a stricter predicate than the FSM, capturing only the highest-accel crossings. The catalog baseline (Step 1) is exact and reproduces Codex numbers perfectly (n=356, mean=0.53%). The inflation and first-crossing measurements should be interpreted as: 'high-accel threshold crossings vs catalog-survived episodes' — the true FSM inflation is likely higher than measured here because more catalog onsets fired at lower accel values that the proxy misses. Conditions implemented: (1) tile-accel_z_5d >= 1.0, (2) >=3/5 tile-accel_z > 0 [sign exact], (3) tile-rs_mom > 0 [exact]. Hysteresis: 5 sessions, matching FSM. Confirmation filter NOT applied (measuring survivorship). Catalog-match window: +-3 sessions.

proxy_coverage_of_catalog.note: Only 37.3% of catalog onset dates have tile-accel_z_5d >= 1.0. Proxy is STRICTER than FSM — it fires at higher absolute accel values than the FSM uses. The 110 matched crossings are a subset of catalog detected by both proxy and FSM.
